chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Sulayman ibn Hilal, from his uncle Abd Allah ibn Hilal, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Trim your mustache and nails every Friday. And if there is nothing to trim, cleanse them, so that leprosy, vitiligo, and madness do not befall you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of trimming the mustache and nails on Friday in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes the regular trimming of the mustache and nails every Friday, elevating it from mere hygiene to a spiritual act of *taharah* (purification) aligned with the weekly rhythm of Shia devotion. The promise of protection from *judham* (leprosy), *baras* (vitiligo), and *junun* (madness) reflects the Shia understanding of the physical-spiritual connection, where bodily cleanliness safeguards against both physical ailments and spiritual impurities. This practice underscores the importance of maintaining the *fitrah* (natural disposition) through consistent, minor acts of worship that prepare the believer for the spiritual intensity of Friday.
